query: For bulk HfNbTaTiZr, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified predictive approach make to overcome the limited accuracy of available analytical predictions and their usual restriction to perfect, defect-free crystals? Address the nearly 0–200 K regime and the 300–1200 K regime, for which measurements also exist on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen; explain why the approach should improve accuracy, predict its advantage over existing analytical approaches, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a held-out conductivity benchmark and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A predictive modeling approach that incorporates oxygen-induced defects and finite-temperature effects in bulk HfNbTaTiZr will yield electrical conductivity predictions that more accurately capture the non-linear temperature dependence observed experimentally in both the cryogenic (0–200 K) and elevated (300–1200 K) regimes, compared to traditional analytical models based on perfect, defect-free crystals.
generation.material_initial_state: Bulk HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy, in its as-cast state and with a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
generation.intervention: Apply a defect-aware predictive framework (e.g., leveraging machine learning and ab initio-informed corrections) that explicitly models point-defect scattering, lattice distortions, and temperature-dependent electron–phonon interactions.
generation.conditions: Electrical conductivity is measured in two temperature regimes: 0–200 K (cryogenic) and 300–1200 K (elevated temperatures).
generation.structural_mediator: Oxygen point defects that generate local lattice distortions and scattering centers.
generation.mechanism: Oxygen impurities introduce additional electron scattering centers, which modify the electronic transport properties by inducing localized states and altering scattering rates. This effect is more pronounced at cryogenic temperatures, influencing weak localization and, at higher temperatures, interfering with phonon scattering dynamics. The predictive approach accounts for these mechanisms explicitly, overcoming limitations of models assuming perfect crystallinity.
generation.predicted_outcome: The defect-aware model will predict conductivity values that deviate by an appreciable margin (e.g., on the order of 10–20% differences) from defect-free analytical predictions, successfully capturing non-linear trends and potential activation-like behavior in the high temperature regime.
generation.baseline: Predictions made using traditional analytical approaches based on perfect, defect-free crystal assumptions.
generation.boundary: The approach is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr alloys measured in the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes and is specifically benchmarked against specimens with 1 wt.% oxygen; predictions outside these temperature ranges or oxygen contents may not be accurate.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative impact of oxygen-induced scattering and the precise magnitude of conductivity deviations remain uncertain due to complexities in defect distribution and temperature-dependent scattering rates.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a systematic series of electrical conductivity measurements on bulk HfNbTaTiZr specimens containing precisely 1 wt.% oxygen across the two specified temperature regimes. Compare these measurements with predictions from both the defect-aware predictive model and traditional defect-free analytical models. Additionally, perform microstructural analyses to confirm the presence and distribution of oxygen-induced defects.
measurements: High-precision conductivity measurements across 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) or atom probe tomography (APT) to characterize oxygen defect distribution.
Electron scattering rate or mobility measurements via spectroscopic techniques (e.g., terahertz spectroscopy).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the experimentally measured conductivity values fall within the error margins predicted by the traditional defect-free models, and no statistically significant improvement in predictive accuracy is observed with the defect-aware model, then the hypothesis is falsified.

## Abstract
The plastic response of the Senkov HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy is explored by means of simulated nanoindentation tests. Both a random alloy and an alloy with chemical short-range order are investigated and compared to the well understood case of an elementary Ta crystal. Strong differences in the dislocation plasticity between the alloys and the elementary Ta crystal are found. The high-entropy alloys show only little relaxation of the indentation dislocation network after indenter retraction and only negligible dislocation emission into the sample interior. Short-range order—besides making the alloy both stiffer and harder—further increases the size of the plastic zone and the dislocation density there. These features are explained by the slow dislocation migration in these alloys. Also, the short-range-ordered alloy features no twinning plasticity in contrast to the random alloy, while elemental Ta exhibits twinning under high stress but detwins considerably under stress relief. The results are in good qualitative agreement with our current knowledge of plasticity in high-entropy alloys.

## Abstract
High-entropy alloys (HEAs) provide new research avenues for alloy combinations in the periodic table, opening numerous possibilities in novel-alloy applications. However, their electrical characteristics have been relatively underexplored. The challenge in establishing an HEA electrical conductivity model lies in the changes in electronic characteristics caused by lattice distortion and complexity of nanostructures. Here we show a low-frequency electrical conductivity model for the Nb-Mo-Ta-W HEA system. The cocktail effect is found to explain trends in electrical-conductivity changes in HEAs, while the magnitude of the reduction is understood by the calculated plasma frequency, free electron density, and measured relaxation time by terahertz spectroscopy. As a result, the refractory HEA Nb15Mo35Ta15W35 thin film exhibits both high hardness and excellent conductivity. This combination of Nb15Mo35Ta15W35 makes it suitable for applications in atomic force microscopy probe coating, significantly improving their wear resistance and atomic-scale image resolution. While first-principles methods have been successfully applied to characterize individual properties of multi-principal element alloys (MPEA), their use in searching for optimal trade-offs between competing properties is hampered by high computational demands. In this work, we present a framework to explore Pareto-optimal compositions by integrating advanced ab initio-based techniques into a Bayesian multi-objective optimization workflow, complemented by a simple analytical model providing straightforward analysis of trends.
